pdfWizardNotice: The original workflow uses the PDF's four lunar tests, data-fitness aggregation and 15 study locations. Scores retain the 0-1 scale: PDF 40.8 equals 0.408. Reported results and proxy data remain labelled.
pdfWizardTargetNotice: M2/M3/M6 use shared Earth-achievable scoring anchors. M4 requires a separate terrain reference for the selected lunar target.
pdf_anchor_sensitivity_available: PDF anchor and task-weight rank sensitivity is available below.
pdf_target_terrain_missing: This target has no imported 30 m / 16 km terrain reference for the PDF's M4 model. Its other tests use shared Earth-achievable anchors; no Connecting Ridge terrain is substituted.
pdfSensitivityIntro: Ranking sensitivity to anchor endpoints +/-20% and alternative task weights. These are deterministic scenarios, separate from network-coverage simulations.
lunarStudyIntro: Explore the team's four-test method with 12 validation sites and three polar examples. Trace every score to a value, a formula and its data fitness.
lunarObjective: Scores express how closely an Earth environment approaches the specified Earth-achievable test anchors. They do not establish physical equivalence to the Moon.
lunarFormulaMeaning: s = feature similarity; c = data fitness (1.0 direct, 0.6 proxy, 0.3 reported judgement, 0 missing); w = normalized importance x uncertainty. Combine within each test, then apply the four test weights.
lunarFunction_histogram: Sum of minimum normalized bin fractions
lunarFunctionsExplained: Histograms are normalized before overlap. Missing values are omitted with c=0, never measured zeros. Negative temperature anchors use the same directed linear formula.
lunarRetiredTitle: Why M1 and M5 were removed
lunarSourcePdf: Read the supplied method PDF (Traditional Chinese)
lunarReferenceScope: This PDF model currently uses Connecting Ridge's slope histogram and 2477 m relief. The other lunar regions' earlier observations remain available separately.
lunarDifferentReference: This shared link selects another lunar reference
lunarDifferentReferenceNote: The link refers to {site}. The PDF model has no independently defined terrain reference for that target yet. Explicitly choose Connecting Ridge or open the earlier observed comparison.
lunarUseReference: Use the PDF's Connecting Ridge reference
lunarRetiredSummary: M1 and M5 are excluded from this study's scoring. Their definitions and results remain archived.
lunarThermalBlock: Share half of M6 weight between its correlated temperatures
lunarFeatureWeightsNote: Defaults are 1 x 1 because the team did not supply numerical I/U values. Each test normalizes its feature weights. These controls are assumptions, not uncertainty estimates.
lunarRankScope: Ranked among the imported study locations only. Data completeness differs across rows; a high partial score does not establish a complete analog.
lunarNoMatches: No imported locations match this filter.
lunarPartialWarning: These are provisional scores of the available evidence. Completeness is the weighted fraction of present features; data fitness also discounts proxies and reported judgements. Neither is a statistical confidence interval or a field-validation certificate.
lunarIceCoverUnknown: Permanent ice cover has not been verified for these windows. An annual-mean temperature threshold cannot classify an ice sheet.
lunarReportedM6: The PDF reports M6 = {score} for this regional example. Recalculation can differ because the document rounds temperatures and the controls change assumptions.
lunarSensitivityNote: Change one endpoint/reference by +/-20% at a time and compare PDF ROC, rank-sum and equal weights. Track rank correlation and top-three frequency; this is not statistical uncertainty propagation.
lunarGlobalNote: The PDF describes {count} land-grid points. Those global POWER and relief files were not in the supplied branch archive, so the website currently contains zero global overall-score cells.
lunarGlobalMapNote: The map and globe show the 15 imported study points, not a completed global heatmap. A global layer will require its own values, quality masks, ice screening and provenance.
lunarObservedArchive: Earlier lunar comparison model: archived reference
lunarDataInventoryNote: The lunar pages use the 2023 MODIS/GIBS monthly LST handoff, ten lunar terrain references and 19599 land cells. POWER and ERA5 are not active lunar temperature inputs. The observed snapshot below belongs to archived comparisons and the current Mars workflow.
lunarValidationSummaryNote: Recomputed from current settings and imported values. AUC is the probability that a sampled first-group score exceeds a second-group score, with half credit for ties. These small hand-selected groups are not independent validation, and feature completeness can differ.
lunarPdfValidation: PDF-reported M6 means: polar 49.5, reference 10.1, control 3.6; reference/control AUC 0.73 and polar/control AUC 1.00. Rounded polar values, unknown checklist entries and changed controls can produce different recalculated results.
tagline:
Our home planet.
A testbed for other worlds.
intro: Start on Earth. Prepare for what comes next. Connect mission requirements to terrestrial sites, and make the strengths and limits of every analog visible.
compareIntro: Earth can reproduce some terrain and processes. Gravity, atmosphere and radiation set clear limits.

lunarMissionIntro: Choose a mission. First explore suitable lunar locations, then compare three new Earth analogs with three least-similar locations.
lunarDetailIntro: One mission, two perspectives: lunar task suitability and Earth analog similarity.
lunarPurposeM2: Test solar power, navigation and vision when sunlight stays close to the horizon.
lunarPurposeM3: Test power storage, insulation and equipment survival through extended darkness and extreme cold.
lunarPurposeM4: Test rover and astronaut mobility over steep slopes, ridges and crater terrain.
lunarPurposeM6: Test prospecting, drilling and handling of ice in cold and potentially frozen ground.
lunarOpenTask: Explore lunar sites and Earth comparisons
lunarRetiredNote: M1 and M5 are excluded by the supplied method. The four retained missions use the team's revised feature weights; task weights matter only for an optional combined score.
lunarWhereOnMoon: Where could this mission be assessed on the Moon?
lunarSuitabilityMeaning: These are preliminary, literature-based team assessments. They guide where to investigate a mission; they do not certify landing safety or operational feasibility.
lunarOtherSites: Other lunar locations — {count} with insufficient evidence

lunarEarthContrast: Earth analogs: two groups for comparison

lunarLeastMeaning: Lowest available task scores within this task's eligible comparison pool.
lunarTieNote: Equal scores are ties; their order follows the source handoff and does not imply a meaningful difference. Place names are approximate grid labels.
lunarValidationMeaning: Established analogs can score higher than the new candidates. They are retained for validation and are not presented as newly discovered sites.
lunarScoreMeaning: A score measures similarity within the Earth-achievable test model, not the probability of mission success or physical equivalence to the Moon.
lunarMissingRule: Missing features are skipped in the weighted score and their availability stays visible. A partial score does not establish complete test coverage.
lunarFitnessMeaning: Data fitness c is 1.0 for direct-derived data, 0.6 for proxies and 0.3 for estimates. It changes the contribution to the score; it is not a statistical confidence level.
lunarSharedAnchor: The scoring anchors are shared Earth extremes, not measured values at this lunar site.
lunarArchiveNote: The new handoff supersedes the earlier 15-site validation model for this lunar experience. Earlier observed and research APIs remain archived separately.
lunarAiDisclosure: The source team discloses Claude assistance for its computations and data assembly. Codex assisted with this website integration and validation.

lunarModisMethodNotice: This task uses 2023 MODIS monthly land-surface temperatures. Maximum/minimum describe monthly means, not daily extremes. Twelve no-LST cells are excluded; polar day-night differences can use the documented zero convention.
marsMissionHeading: Find an Earth analog for Mars
marsMissionIntro: Choose a test and a Mars study area, then compare measured Earth environments.
marsIceRule: R3 and R5 require SWIM Ci ≥ 0.1. This target does not meet that condition; no ranking is assigned.
marsR2Reason: Global image texture and dune-fraction data are unavailable. R2 remains unscored; Sentinel-2 and Mars CTX/MGD3 are needed for a later local study.
marsScoreMeaning: Scores use an equal-weight geometric mean of feature similarities, with a 0.01 floor. A weak feature lowers the result. Compare ranks within the same test; different tests measure different requirements.
marsRequired: Every feature applicable to the selected target is required. Missing features prevent scoring. R2 is unscored; R3/R5 are restricted to ice targets.
marsConditional: ASTER mineral indices apply to Jezero, Arcadia and AP-105. Glacier distance applies only to Protonilus. These target-specific features are required where applicable.
marsCoordinateNote: Coordinates and study radii follow the supplied Mars handoff. They describe regional study areas.
marsUnknownSite: This shared Mars target is not in the current seven-site handoff. Choose a current target in step 2.
marsResponseMismatch: The response does not match the selected target, tests or data version. Retry after the services finish updating.
marsPlaceNote: Coordinates identify each 0.1° Earth cell. Place labels are automatic nearest-town references, not surveyed site names.
marsRankingScope: {count} fully scored land cells; new candidates exclude locations within 50 km of known analogs and are at least 150 km apart.
marsGridMeaning: Each 1° map cell shows the highest scored 0.1° land cell inside it. Blank cells have no score. This is a regional screen.
marsKnownRule: Known analogs are kept separate from new candidates. Locations within 50 km of a known analog are flagged.
marsKnownMedian: Validation scores are medians over each known site's study area. The export has no per-feature evidence for these regional medians.
marsProfileMeaning: A separate reference compares five dimensions: terrain, surface, environment, water/ice and dust. Dimension and overall scores use geometric means. Ranking requires ≥80% of dimensions and variables. Temperature and aridity reward Earth extremes; biology and subsurface are not scored.
marsProfileOpen: View overall top 10 and top 5 by dimension
marsNetworkRule: A site covers a requirement when its score reaches 90% of that requirement's best score. The network minimizes the number of Earth cells needed for your selected scored tests.
marsPoolScope: Computed exactly within the supplied 3,317-cell candidate pool. The global 0.1° raster is not part of the handoff.
marsGlobalNetwork: All seven Mars targets: the supplied 27-demand network
marsValidationSummary: For {pairs} known-analog/dimension pairs, the median global top percentage is {percent}%. None of {controls} negative-control cases entered the top 25%.
marsStability: The supplied sensitivity analysis reports stability ≥0.8 for 64 of 70 profile top-ten sites. This assesses ranking stability, not landing safety.
marsDataScope: Imported from the team's 15 November 2026 Mars handoff: seven Mars targets, 27 scored target/test pairs, a 17,225-cell display grid and a 3,317-cell planning pool. Feature evidence is shown where exported.

marsPurpose_R4: Compare exposed rock and mineral proxies.
marsPurpose_R6: Compare dust, temperature and seasonal behavior.

lunarWeightOriginTitle: Where the feature weights come from
lunarWeightOriginIntro: The team chose these initial weights from the purpose of each test. They are not official NASA weights, not fitted to the current ranking, and not yet validated by a dedicated ranking-sensitivity test of these weight choices.
lunarWeightEffectiveMeaning: Data fitness c adjusts the design weight: 1.0 for direct-derived inputs, 0.6 for proxies and 0.3 for estimates. The effective column is the normalized coefficient among observed features, not each feature's earned score or statistical confidence. Missing features are omitted.
lunarWeightDesignOnly: This is the design-only expression after transforming inputs to similarities from 0 to 1. It equals the website's fitness-adjusted score only when all features are observed and their c values are equal.
lunarWeightFullMethod: Read the full rationale, anchors and equations
lunarWeightReason_M2: Low-angle daylight receives 70% because it measures the annual opportunity to test low-angle power and long shadows. Representative noon elevation receives 30% as supporting information about whether the Sun remains low at its highest daily position. Both depend on latitude; reducing the noon weight limits, but does not eliminate, overlapping information. The rationale supports a larger daylight-fraction weight, not a uniquely optimal 70%.
lunarWeightLimits_M2: Noon elevation uses 90° and 5° as zero/full-score anchors; the current representative is equinox noon. The low-angle fraction counts annual daylight hours with solar elevation between 0° and 10° and excludes night from its denominator. Both current fitness coefficients are 1.0, so effective weights remain 30% and 70%.
lunarWeightReason_M3: Half of the design weight goes to continuous darkness, which directly addresses surviving at least 120 hours without sunlight. The thermal half is split 70:30 between extreme cold and cycling, yielding 35% for minimum temperature and 15% for day-night range. A hot desert can have a large range without providing extreme-cold conditions.
lunarWeightLimits_M3: A high weighted score does not prove the 120-hour condition or simultaneous darkness and extreme cold. Current temperatures are monthly MODIS surface-temperature statistics, not 2 m air temperature, instantaneous annual extremes or measured equipment-surface cycles. With c = 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.6, the full-data effective weights are 62.5% / 26.25% / 11.25%.
lunarWeightReason_M4: Slope distribution receives 70% because it describes the uphill/downhill conditions experienced by vehicles and people. Relief within 16 km receives 30% to retain the region's vertical scale. Equal relief can come from a long gentle slope or a local cliff; similar slope histograms can still describe different terrain scales.
lunarWeightLimits_M4: The two inputs need consistent study support and comparable DEM resolution. Current references use 30 m slope distributions and 16 km windows. A high statistical match does not establish a connected traversable route. Both fitness coefficients are 1.0, so effective weights remain 70% and 30%.
lunarWeightReason_M6: The mean-temperature background and warmest conditions each receive 25%, together making up the thermal half. Ice/permafrost receives 50% because the resource itself is more directly related to detection and excavation than cold temperature alone. A low annual mean must not hide warm-season conditions.
lunarWeightLimits_M6: The current third feature is an uncalibrated LST-based frozen-ground proxy, not a field checklist or confirmed ice. Mean and maximum values are monthly MODIS surface-temperature statistics. With c = 0.6 / 0.6 / 0.3, all three w·c products are 0.15: the effective full-data weights are one third each. The earlier two-temperature 50:50 proposal is not this three-feature model.
lunarDarknessMet: Continuous-darkness check: {hours} h — meets the ≥120 h duration condition. This does not establish simultaneous extreme cold.
lunarDarknessNotMet: Continuous-darkness check: {hours} h — below the 120 h duration condition, regardless of the aggregate score.
lunarDarknessUnknown: Continuous-darkness check: no usable duration is available to assess the 120 h condition.
